description: seed_species.py exists and defines exactly 18 seed species
steps: Step 1: Import seed_species from config module
Step 2: Verify SEED_SPECIES is a list
Step 3: Assert len(SEED_SPECIES) == 18
Step 4: Verify all entries have species_key, scientific_name, wikipedia_title

description: Each seed species entry has valid species_key format (slugified scientific name)
steps: Step 1: For each species in SEED_SPECIES, check species_key is lowercase
Step 2: Verify underscores replace spaces in species_key
Step 3: Verify species_key matches slugify(scientific_name)
Step 4: Verify no special characters in species_key

description: Each seed species has valid scientific_name (binomial format)
steps: Step 1: Verify each scientific_name contains exactly two words (genus + species)
Step 2: Verify genus is capitalized
Step 3: Verify species epithet is lowercase
Step 4: Verify no trailing/leading whitespace

description: Each seed species has a valid Wikipedia title
steps: Step 1: For each species, assert wikipedia_title is a non-empty string
Step 2: Verify wikipedia_title does not contain underscores (uses spaces)
Step 3: Verify title is in English
Step 4: Verify title matches Wikipedia page naming convention

description: pyproject.toml specifies Python >=3.11
steps: Step 1: Read pyproject.toml
Step 2: Find requires-python field
Step 3: Verify requires-python specifies >=3.11
Step 4: Verify Python version in environment meets requirement

description: slugify function converts scientific names to species_key deterministically
steps: Step 1: Import slugify function
Step 2: Call slugify('Carcharodon carcharias')
Step 3: Assert result is 'carcharodon_carcharias'
Step 4: Verify output is lowercase with underscores

description: slugify handles multi-word scientific names correctly
steps: Step 1: Call slugify('Carcharodon carcharias')
Step 2: Assert result is 'carcharodon_carcharias'
Step 3: Verify no extra characters or spaces remain
Step 4: Verify all 18 seed species keys are producible via slugify

description: Wikipedia title resolution follows redirects to final article title
steps: Step 1: Call Wikipedia resolve function with a known redirect title
Step 2: Verify function follows redirect
Step 3: Assert resolved_via includes 'REDIRECT'
Step 4: Verify final title is the canonical Wikipedia article title

description: Wikipedia title resolution uses search when direct title doesn't match
steps: Step 1: Call resolve function with scientific name (not Wikipedia title)
Step 2: Verify function searches Wikipedia API
Step 3: Assert resolved_via includes 'SEARCH'
Step 4: Verify returned page URL is valid

description: Wikipedia resolution detects ambiguous results and sets AMBIGUOUS_RESOLUTION
steps: Step 1: Call resolve function with a name that maps to multiple candidates
Step 2: Verify function returns rejection with AMBIGUOUS_RESOLUTION
Step 3: Assert no title is returned
Step 4: Verify candidates are logged for debugging

description: Wikipedia resolution returns PAGE_NOT_FOUND when no article exists
steps: Step 1: Call resolve function with nonexistent title
Step 2: Verify function returns rejection with PAGE_NOT_FOUND
Step 3: Assert no page metadata is returned
Step 4: Verify error is documented for cuarentena

description: Wikipedia resolution detects disambiguation pages
steps: Step 1: Call resolve function with a disambiguation page title
Step 2: Verify is_disambiguation flag is True
Step 3: Assert DISAMBIGUATION_PAGE rejection is documented
Step 4: Verify disambiguation page is rejected, not accepted

description: Bronze GBIF Species Match fetches taxonomy data via API
steps: Step 1: Send GET to https://api.gbif.org/v1/species/match?name=Carcharodon carcharias
Step 2: Verify HTTP 200 response
Step 3: Assert response contains usageKey, scientificName, matchType, kingdom, phylum, class
Step 4: Verify response is valid JSON

description: Bronze GBIF Species Match handles non-EXACT matches gracefully
steps: Step 1: Query GBIF Species Match with an ambiguous or partial name
Step 2: Verify HTTP 200 response
Step 3: Assert matchType is not 'EXACT'
Step 4: Verify raw response is preserved as-is

description: Bronze GBIF Species Match persists raw JSON with metadata envelope
steps: Step 1: Call bronze GBIF taxonomy pipeline for a species
Step 2: Find the output JSON file in data/bronze/gbif_taxonomy/
Step 3: Verify file contains 'source', 'lote', 'ingested_at', 'species_queried', 'raw_responses'
Step 4: Assert 'source' field is 'gbif_taxonomy'

description: Bronze GBIF Species Match file naming includes batch number and ISO timestamp
steps: Step 1: Run GBIF taxonomy fetch for batch 1
Step 2: Verify filename matches pattern lote_1__{YYYY-MM-DD}T{HH-MM-SS}Z.json
Step 3: Assert timestamp uses ISO 8601 format
Step 4: Verify file is in data/bronze/gbif_taxonomy/ directory

description: Bronze GBIF Species Match persists HTTP errors without transformation
steps: Step 1: Simulate HTTP error from GBIF Species Match API
Step 2: Verify file is still written to bronze
Step 3: Assert raw error response is preserved in raw_responses
Step 4: Verify envelope metadata is still populated

description: Bronze GBIF Occurrence Search fetches occurrence records with correct parameters
steps: Step 1: Send GET to GBIF Occurrence Search with scientificName, hasCoordinate=true, limit=50
Step 2: Verify HTTP 200 response
Step 3: Assert response contains 'results' array
Step 4: Verify each result has gbifID, decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude

description: Bronze GBIF Occurrence Search limit defaults to 50 records
steps: Step 1: Query GBIF Occurrence Search without explicit limit
Step 2: Verify default limit of 50 is applied
Step 3: Assert results count <= 50 per query
Step 4: Verify query parameter includes limit=50

description: Bronze GBIF Occurrence persists raw JSON with metadata envelope
steps: Step 1: Call bronze GBIF occurrence pipeline for a species
Step 2: Find output file in data/bronze/gbif_occurrence/
Step 3: Verify envelope has source='gbif_occurrence', lote, ingested_at, species_queried, raw_responses
Step 4: Assert raw responses are complete and untransformed

description: Bronze GBIF Occurrence handles empty results gracefully
steps: Step 1: Query GBIF Occurrence with a rare species that has few or no records
Step 2: Verify HTTP 200 with empty results array
Step 3: Assert raw_responses is persisted as-is
Step 4: Verify envelope still has all required metadata fields

description: Bronze GBIF Occurrence persists error responses without transformation
steps: Step 1: Simulate GBIF Occurrence API failure
Step 2: Verify file is written to bronze
Step 3: Assert raw error response is in raw_responses
Step 4: Verify envelope metadata is present

description: Bronze GBIF Occurrence includes hasCoordinate=true parameter
steps: Step 1: Verify request URL includes hasCoordinate=true
Step 2: Assert only records with coordinates are returned
Step 3: Verify each result has non-null coordinates
Step 4: Check coordinate_uncertainty_m is present if available

description: Bronze Wikipedia fetches summary via REST API
steps: Step 1: Send GET to https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/summary/Great white shark
Step 2: Verify HTTP 200 response
Step 3: Assert response contains title, extract, page_url
Step 4: Verify response is valid JSON

description: Bronze Wikipedia fetches full extracts via action API
steps: Step 1: Send GET to Wikipedia action API with titles=Great white shark
Step 2: Verify HTTP 200 response
Step 3: Assert response contains query.pages with extract content
Step 4: Verify explaintext=true returns plain text (no HTML/markup)

description: Bronze Wikipedia persists raw responses with metadata envelope
steps: Step 1: Call bronze Wikipedia pipeline for a species
Step 2: Find output file in data/bronze/wikipedia/
Step 3: Verify envelope has source='wikipedia', lote, ingested_at, species_queried, raw_responses
Step 4: Assert summary and extracts responses are both preserved

description: Bronze Wikipedia file naming includes batch number and ISO timestamp
steps: Step 1: Run Wikipedia fetch for batch 1
Step 2: Verify filename matches lote_1__{YYYY-MM-DD}T{HH-MM-SS}Z.json
Step 3: Assert file is in data/bronze/wikipedia/ directory
Step 4: Verify a second batch produces lote_2 filename

description: Bronze Wikipedia persists error responses without transformation
steps: Step 1: Fetch a nonexistent Wikipedia page
Step 2: Verify HTTP 404 response is preserved in raw_responses
Step 3: Assert envelope metadata is populated
Step 4: Verify file is written to bronze

description: Bronze supports at least 2 distinct batches per source
steps: Step 1: Fetch data for Lote 1 across all 3 sources
Step 2: Verify files exist in each source directory with lote_1 prefix
Step 3: Fetch data for Lote 2 with different species
Step 4: Verify files exist with lote_2 prefix in each source directory

description: Bronze raw_responses preserves query and response pairs for each species
steps: Step 1: Open a bronze JSON file with multiple species queries
Step 2: Assert raw_responses is a list of objects
Step 3: Verify each object has 'query' and 'response' fields
Step 4: Verify the response field contains the full API response

description: Bronze directory structure is created automatically
steps: Step 1: Check data/bronze/ exists
Step 2: Verify subdirectories: gbif_taxonomy/, gbif_occurrence/, wikipedia/
Step 3: Assert directories are created if missing
Step 4: Verify data/.gitignore inside data/ (if needed)

description: Bronze ingestion timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with Z suffix
steps: Step 1: Read ingested_at from a bronze file envelope
Step 2: Assert format matches YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ
Step 3: Parse as ISO 8601 datetime (should not error)
Step 4: Verify timestamp corresponds to actual ingestion time

description: Bronze raw JSON files are valid JSON and can be parsed
steps: Step 1: Open each bronze file and parse with json.load()
Step 2: Assert no parsing errors
Step 3: Verify required envelope fields present
Step 4: Verify content matches expected structure

description: WikipediaPage Pydantic model validates species_key as string
steps: Step 1: Create WikipediaPage with valid species_key
Step 2: Verify model is valid
Step 3: Create WikipediaPage without species_key
Step 4: Assert validation error is raised

description: WikipediaPage Pydantic model validates title as non-empty string
steps: Step 1: Create WikipediaPage with valid title
Step 2: Create WikipediaPage with empty title
Step 3: Assert validation error for empty title
Step 4: Verify title is stored correctly

description: WikipediaPage Pydantic model validates resolved_via field
steps: Step 1: Create WikipediaPage with resolved_via='DIRECT_TITLE'
Step 2: Create WikipediaPage with resolved_via='SEARCH'
Step 3: Create WikipediaPage with resolved_via='REDIRECT'
Step 4: Verify all three are accepted

description: WikipediaPage extract validation requires minimum 50 characters
steps: Step 1: Create WikipediaPage with extract < 50 characters
Step 2: Verify validation error for EXTRACT_TOO_SHORT
Step 3: Create WikipediaPage with extract >= 50 characters
Step 4: Verify passes validation

description: WikipediaPage validates sections_text as string
steps: Step 1: Create WikipediaPage with valid sections_text
Step 2: Create WikipediaPage with empty sections_text
Step 3: Assert MISSING_SECTIONS_TEXT rejection
Step 4: Verify sections with content pass validation

description: WikipediaPage validates page_url as valid URL
steps: Step 1: Create WikipediaPage with valid Wikipedia URL
Step 2: Verify URL is accepted
Step 3: Create WikipediaPage with invalid URL
Step 4: Assert validation error

description: WikipediaPage is_disambiguation field defaults to False
steps: Step 1: Create WikipediaPage without specifying is_disambiguation
Step 2: Assert is_disambiguation is False
Step 3: Create WikipediaPage with is_disambiguation=True
Step 4: Verify boolean field is stored correctly

description: Silver Wikipedia rejects PAGE_NOT_FOUND and documents reason
steps: Step 1: Process a Wikipedia page that does not exist
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is PAGE_NOT_FOUND
Step 3: Assert rejected file is written with batch_id prefix
Step 4: Verify rejected file contains enough context to diagnose

description: Silver Wikipedia rejects AMBIGUOUS_RESOLUTION and documents reason
steps: Step 1: Process a species name that maps to multiple Wikipedia candidates
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is AMBIGUOUS_RESOLUTION
Step 3: Assert rejected file is written with details
Step 4: Verify multiple candidate titles are documented

description: Silver Wikipedia rejects EXTRACT_TOO_SHORT and documents reason
steps: Step 1: Process a Wikipedia page with extract under 50 chars
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is EXTRACT_TOO_SHORT
Step 3: Assert extract length is documented
Step 4: Verify invalid file is written to rejected/

description: Silver Wikipedia rejects DISAMBIGUATION_PAGE and documents reason
steps: Step 1: Process a Wikipedia page that is a disambiguation page
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is DISAMBIGUATION_PAGE
Step 3: Assert disambiguation flag is documented
Step 4: Verify rejected file includes original page metadata

description: Silver Wikipedia rejects HTTP_ERROR and documents reason
steps: Step 1: Simulate HTTP error from Wikipedia API
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is HTTP_ERROR
Step 3: Assert HTTP status code is documented
Step 4: Verify rejected file is written

description: Silver Wikipedia rejects MISSING_SECTIONS_TEXT and documents reason
steps: Step 1: Process Wikipedia page that returns no sections text
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is MISSING_SECTIONS_TEXT
Step 3: Assert rejected file is written
Step 4: Verify context about missing sections is included

description: Silver valid Wikipedia records saved as individual JSON files by species_key
steps: Step 1: Process a valid Wikipedia page
Step 2: Verify file created at data/silver/wikipedia/valid/{species_key}.json
Step 3: Assert file is valid JSON matching WikipediaPage schema
Step 4: Verify no extra fields are present

description: Silver rejected Wikipedia records saved with batch_id prefix
steps: Step 1: Process an invalid Wikipedia page
Step 2: Verify file at data/silver/wikipedia/rejected/{batch_id}_wikipedia_{key}.json
Step 3: Assert file contains rejection_reason field
Step 4: Verify file contains original data context

description: GBIFTaxonomy model validates usage_key as int
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFTaxonomy with valid usage_key integer
Step 2: Create GBIFTaxonomy with non-integer usage_key
Step 3: Assert validation error for non-integer
Step 4: Verify usage_key is stored correctly

description: GBIFTaxonomy model validates scientific_name and canonical_name
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFTaxonomy with valid names
Step 2: Assert passes validation
Step 3: Create with empty scientific_name
Step 4: Assert validation error

description: GBIFTaxonomy model validates rank field
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFTaxonomy with valid rank (e.g. 'SPECIES')
Step 2: Verify rank is accepted
Step 3: Assert rank is stored as string
Step 4: Verify rank can be None if not provided

description: GBIFTaxonomy model validates match_type only accepts 'EXACT' for MATCHED status
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFTaxonomy with match_type='EXACT'
Step 2: Create GBIFTaxonomy with match_type='FUZZY'
Step 3: Verify both are valid Pydantic models
Step 4: Assert match_type is stored as string

description: GBIFTaxonomy model validates confidence as int
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFTaxonomy with confidence=100
Step 2: Assert passes validation
Step 3: Create with negative confidence
Step 4: Assert validation error or behavior is defined

description: GBIFTaxonomy accepts optional kingdom, phylum, class_name
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFTaxonomy with kingdom, phylum, class_name provided
Step 2: Assert passes validation
Step 3: Create without these optional fields
Step 4: Verify defaults to None

description: Silver GBIF Taxonomy rejects MATCH_TYPE_NOT_EXACT when match_type != 'EXACT'
steps: Step 1: Process GBIF taxonomy with match_type='FUZZY'
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is MATCH_TYPE_NOT_EXACT
Step 3: Assert species is marked UNMATCHED
Step 4: Verify rejected file is written

description: Silver GBIF Taxonomy rejects NO_MATCH_RETURNED when GBIF returns no candidates
steps: Step 1: Query GBIF Species Match with a nonexistent species name
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is NO_MATCH_RETURNED
Step 3: Assert rejected file is written
Step 4: Verify context is documented

description: Silver GBIF Taxonomy rejects HTTP_ERROR on API failure
steps: Step 1: Simulate HTTP error from GBIF Species Match
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is HTTP_ERROR
Step 3: Assert HTTP status code is documented
Step 4: Verify rejected file is written

description: Silver valid GBIF Taxonomy saved as individual JSON by species_key
steps: Step 1: Process valid GBIF taxonomy response (match_type='EXACT')
Step 2: Verify file at data/silver/gbif_taxonomy/valid/{species_key}.json
Step 3: Assert file matches GBIFTaxonomy schema
Step 4: Verify no extra fields

description: Silver rejected GBIF Taxonomy saved with batch_id prefix
steps: Step 1: Process invalid GBIF taxonomy response
Step 2: Verify file at data/silver/gbif_taxonomy/rejected/{batch_id}_gbif_taxonomy_{key}.json
Step 3: Assert file contains rejection_reason
Step 4: Verify original data context

description: GBIFOccurrence model validates gbif_id as int (clave natural)
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFOccurrence with valid int gbif_id
Step 2: Create GBIFOccurrence without gbif_id
Step 3: Assert MISSING_GBIF_ID rejection
Step 4: Create with non-int gbif_id and assert error

description: GBIFOccurrence model validates decimal_latitude in range [-90, 90]
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFOccurrence with decimal_latitude=45.0
Step 2: Assert passes
Step 3: Create with decimal_latitude=100.0
Step 4: Assert COORDINATES_OUT_OF_RANGE

description: GBIFOccurrence model validates decimal_longitude in range [-180, 180]
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFOccurrence with decimal_longitude=90.0
Step 2: Assert passes
Step 3: Create with decimal_longitude=200.0
Step 4: Assert COORDINATES_OUT_OF_RANGE

description: GBIFOccurrence model validates basis_of_record as string
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFOccurrence with valid basis_of_record (e.g. 'HUMAN_OBSERVATION')
Step 2: Assert passes
Step 3: Create without basis_of_record
Step 4: Assert MISSING_BASIS_OF_RECORD

description: GBIFOccurrence model accepts optional country
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFOccurrence with country='South Africa'
Step 2: Assert passes
Step 3: Create without country
Step 4: Verify it defaults to None

description: GBIFOccurrence model accepts optional event_date as datetime
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFOccurrence with valid event_date
Step 2: Assert passes
Step 3: Create with invalid date string
Step 4: Assert INVALID_EVENT_DATE

description: GBIFOccurrence model accepts optional iucn_red_list_category
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFOccurrence with iucn_red_list_category='VULNERABLE'
Step 2: Assert passes
Step 3: Create without it
Step 4: Verify defaults to None

description: GBIFOccurrence model accepts optional coordinate_uncertainty_m as float
steps: Step 1: Create GBIFOccurrence with coordinate_uncertainty_m=100.5
Step 2: Assert passes
Step 3: Create without it
Step 4: Verify defaults to None

description: Silver GBIF Occurrence rejects MISSING_COORDINATES when lat/lon is null
steps: Step 1: Process occurrence with null/None decimal_latitude
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is MISSING_COORDINATES
Step 3: Assert rejected file is written
Step 4: Verify occurrence context is preserved

description: Silver GBIF Occurrence rejects COORDINATES_OUT_OF_RANGE for invalid lat/lon
steps: Step 1: Process occurrence with decimal_latitude=95.0
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is COORDINATES_OUT_OF_RANGE
Step 3: Assert rejected file is written
Step 4: Process occurrence with decimal_longitude=200.0 and verify same

description: Silver GBIF Occurrence rejects MISSING_GBIF_ID when gbif_id is null
steps: Step 1: Process occurrence without gbifID
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is MISSING_GBIF_ID
Step 3: Assert rejected file is written
Step 4: Verify occurrence data is preserved

description: Silver GBIF Occurrence rejects INVALID_EVENT_DATE for unparseable dates
steps: Step 1: Process occurrence with eventDate='not-a-date'
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is INVALID_EVENT_DATE
Step 3: Assert rejected file is written
Step 4: Process occurrence with null eventDate (should be allowed)

description: Silver GBIF Occurrence rejects MISSING_BASIS_OF_RECORD
steps: Step 1: Process occurrence with null/empty basisOfRecord
Step 2: Verify rejection reason is MISSING_BASIS_OF_RECORD
Step 3: Assert rejected file is written
Step 4: Verify original fields preserved

description: Silver valid GBIF Occurrences saved as individual JSON by gbif_id
steps: Step 1: Process valid occurrence records
Step 2: Verify files at data/silver/gbif_occurrence/valid/{gbif_id}.json
Step 3: Assert files match GBIFOccurrence schema
Step 4: Verify no extra fields

description: Silver rejected GBIF Occurrences saved with batch_id prefix
steps: Step 1: Process invalid occurrence
Step 2: Verify file at data/silver/gbif_occurrence/rejected/{batch_id}_gbif_occurrence_{key}.json
Step 3: Assert file contains rejection_reason
Step 4: Verify context preserved

description: Silver directory structure is created for all sources (valid + rejected)
steps: Step 1: Check data/silver/wikipedia/valid/ exists
Step 2: Check data/silver/wikipedia/rejected/ exists
Step 3: Check data/silver/gbif_taxonomy/valid/ and rejected/ exist
Step 4: Check data/silver/gbif_occurrence/valid/ and rejected/ exist

description: Merge requires Wikipedia as mandatory pivot (1:1 cardinality per species)
steps: Step 1: Run merge on a species with valid Wikipedia data
Step 2: Verify merge output includes Wikipedia fields
Step 3: Run merge trying to introduce species without Wikipedia
Step 4: Assert species is not added to species_catalog

description: Species without valid Wikipedia are not added to species_catalog
steps: Step 1: Attempt merge for a species with no valid Wikipedia page
Step 2: Verify species_key is NOT in species_catalog after merge
Step 3: Assert warning is documented in gold_build_log
Step 4: Verify species can be retried in a future batch

description: GBIF never introduces a species_key that doesn't exist in Wikipedia
steps: Step 1: Provide only GBIF data (no Wikipedia) for an unknown species
Step 2: Verify merge does not create a new species_key
Step 3: Assert species_catalog is unchanged
Step 4: Verify pipeline continues processing other species

description: GBIF Taxonomy joined by species_key only when match_type is EXACT
steps: Step 1: Process species with valid Wikipedia + GBIF EXACT match
Step 2: Verify taxonomy fields (kingdom, phylum, class, rank) are populated
Step 3: Assert taxonomy_status = 'MATCHED'
Step 4: Verify species_key is used as join key

description: Non-EXACT GBIF Taxonomy results in UNMATCHED status (species still valid via Wikipedia)
steps: Step 1: Process species with valid Wikipedia + GBIF non-EXACT match
Step 2: Verify taxonomy fields are null/None
Step 3: Assert taxonomy_status = 'UNMATCHED'
Step 4: Verify species is still valid and added to catalog via Wikipedia

description: GBIF Occurrence aggregated 1:N -> 1:1 summary per species
steps: Step 1: Process species with multiple GBIF occurrence records
Step 2: Verify merge output has single occurrence summary
Step 3: Assert n_occurrences_validas matches count of valid occurrences
Step 4: Verify paises contains unique country names ordered by frequency

description: GBIFOccurrenceSummary includes n_occurrences_validas count
steps: Step 1: Process species with 5 valid occurrences
Step 2: Verify n_occurrences_validas = 5
Step 3: Process species with 0 valid occurrences
Step 4: Verify n_occurrences_validas = 0 and augmentation empty

description: GBIFOccurrenceSummary paises ordered by frequency descending
steps: Step 1: Process species with occurrences from countries A, B, A, C, B, A
Step 2: Verify paises list has 'A' first (most frequent)
Step 3: Verify no duplicate country names in list
Step 4: Verify counts are consistent with raw occurrence data

description: GBIFOccurrenceSummary anio_min and anio_max from occurrence date range
steps: Step 1: Process species with occurrences dated 2010, 2015, 2020
Step 2: Verify anio_min = 2010
Step 3: Verify anio_max = 2020
Step 4: Process species with no dates and verify anio_min/anio_max are None

description: GBIFOccurrenceSummary iucn_red_list_category uses mode (most frequent)
steps: Step 1: Process species with IUCN categories: VU, VU, NT
Step 2: Verify iucn_red_list_category = 'VULNERABLE'
Step 3: For tie, verify most recent event_date determines winner
Step 4: Process with no IUCN data and verify category is None

description: Zero valid occurrences results in GBIF_AUGMENTATION_EMPTY (not an error)
steps: Step 1: Process species with 0 valid occurrences
Step 2: Verify augmentation_status = 'GBIF_AUGMENTATION_EMPTY'
Step 3: Assert species is still valid via Wikipedia
Step 4: Verify occurrence summary has default empty values

description: Merge output record contains all required fields
steps: Step 1: Process a complete species through merge
Step 2: Verify output has: species_key, wikipedia_title, extract, sections_text
Step 3: Verify output has: kingdom, phylum, class_name, rank, taxonomy_status
Step 4: Verify output has: n_occurrences_validas, paises, anio_min, anio_max, iucn_red_list_category, augmentation_status

description: DuckDB file is created at data/warehouse.duckdb after first warehouse operation
steps: Step 1: Run warehouse load for a batch
Step 2: Verify data/warehouse.duckdb file exists
Step 3: Assert it is a valid DuckDB database
Step 4: Verify it can be opened with duckdb.connect()

description: silver_wikipedia table created with species_key as PRIMARY KEY
steps: Step 1: Connect to DuckDB and check table schema
Step 2: Verify silver_wikipedia table exists
Step 3: Assert species_key is PRIMARY KEY
Step 4: Verify it has all WikipediaPage fields as columns

description: silver_gbif_taxonomy table created with species_key as PRIMARY KEY
steps: Step 1: Connect to DuckDB and check table schema
Step 2: Verify silver_gbif_taxonomy table exists
Step 3: Assert species_key is PRIMARY KEY
Step 4: Verify all GBIFTaxonomy fields are columns

description: silver_gbif_occurrences table created with gbif_id as PRIMARY KEY
steps: Step 1: Connect to DuckDB and check table schema
Step 2: Verify silver_gbif_occurrences table exists
Step 3: Assert gbif_id is PRIMARY KEY
Step 4: Verify all GBIFOccurrence fields are columns

description: species_merged table created with species_key as PRIMARY KEY
steps: Step 1: Connect to DuckDB and check table schema
Step 2: Verify species_merged table exists
Step 3: Assert species_key is PRIMARY KEY
Step 4: Verify all merge output fields are columns

description: species_catalog table created with species_key as PRIMARY KEY
steps: Step 1: Connect to DuckDB and check table schema
Step 2: Verify species_catalog table exists
Step 3: Assert species_key is PRIMARY KEY
Step 4: Verify schema matches: scientific_name, wikipedia_title, first_seen_batch_id, first_processed_at, last_processed_at, origin

description: species_catalog origin field is 'SEED' for seed species processed first time
steps: Step 1: Process seed batch through full pipeline
Step 2: Query species_catalog for a seed species
Step 3: Assert origin = 'SEED'
Step 4: Verify all 18 seed species have origin='SEED'

description: species_catalog origin field is 'AD_HOC' for non-seed species
steps: Step 1: Process a non-seed species (new species) through pipeline
Step 2: Query species_catalog for that species
Step 3: Assert origin = 'AD_HOC'
Step 4: Verify first_seen_batch_id documents the batch

description: UPSERT pattern uses ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (not INSERT-only)
steps: Step 1: Inspect warehouse INSERT statements
Step 2: Verify they use ON CONFLICT (PK) DO UPDATE
Step 3: Assert SET clause includes all relevant columns
Step 4: Verify updated_at is set to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP

description: species_catalog upserts update last_processed_at on conflict
steps: Step 1: Process a species through pipeline
Step 2: Record last_processed_at
Step 3: Reprocess the same species after a short delay
Step 4: Verify last_processed_at is updated (newer timestamp)

description: First-time species processed and inserted into species_merged
steps: Step 1: Verify species_merged is initially empty
Step 2: Process one species through pipeline
Step 3: Query species_merged for that species_key
Step 4: Assert record exists with all merge fields populated

description: species_catalog records first_seen_batch_id on first insert
steps: Step 1: Process batch 'seed_batch_1' through pipeline
Step 2: Query species_catalog for processed species
Step 3: Assert first_seen_batch_id = 'seed_batch_1'
Step 4: Verify first_processed_at is populated

description: All 5 warehouse tables are populated after pipeline execution
steps: Step 1: Execute full pipeline for a batch
Step 2: Query row count for silver_wikipedia
Step 3: Query row count for silver_gbif_taxonomy, silver_gbif_occurrences, species_merged, species_catalog
Step 4: Assert all tables have > 0 rows

description: Warehouse UPSERT correctly updates existing records with new data
steps: Step 1: Process batch with initial data
Step 2: Modify Wikipedia content for a species
Step 3: Reprocess same batch
Step 4: Verify species_merged.extract reflects updated content

description: Idempotency evidence: rows_new = 0 on second consecutive run of same batch
steps: Step 1: Run full pipeline on Batch 1, record evidence
Step 2: Run full pipeline on identical Batch 1 again
Step 3: Query evidence table for second run
Step 4: Assert filas_nuevas = 0 for all 5 tables

description: Idempotency evidence table shows rows_before, rows_after, rows_new, rows_updated
steps: Step 1: Run pipeline and generate evidence
